speeches.speaker: Jan McLucas
speeches.brief: The Same-Sex Relationships (Equal Treatment in Commonwealth Laws—General Law Reform) Bill 2008 amends 68 Commonwealth laws to remove discrimination against same-sex couples and their children, introduces a standard definition of de facto partner, and addresses marital status discrimination, with most amendments commencing the day after royal assent and all by mid-2009.

speeches.speaker: Glenn Sterle
speeches.brief: The Legal and Constitutional Affairs Committee report on the Same-Sex Relationships (Equal Treatment in Commonwealth Laws—General Law Reform) Bill 2008 was presented and ordered to be printed.

speeches.speaker: George Brandis
speeches.brief: The opposition supported the Same-Sex Relationships (Equal Treatment in Commonwealth Laws—General Law Reform) Bill 2008, which amends 68 Commonwealth laws to eliminate discrimination against same-sex couples and their children. Speakers from the opposition, Greens, and Labor noted the reforms as historic, with the Greens also calling for a conscience vote on same-sex marriage.

speeches.speaker: Dana Wortley
speeches.brief: The Same-Sex Relationships (Equal Treatment in Commonwealth Laws—General Law Reform) Bill 2008 amends 68 federal laws to eliminate discrimination against same-sex couples and their children, implementing Labor’s election commitment and recommendations from the Australian Human Rights Commission’s 2007 report. Supporters argued it ensures equal treatment under law, while opponents, including Family First and Senator Joyce, claimed it undermines marriage and children’s rights.

speeches.speaker: Penny Wong
speeches.brief: The Greens senator moved amendments to remove discrimination against same-sex couples, including inserting "or couple" into definitions in the Sex Discrimination Act and redefining marriage in the Marriage Act as between "two persons, regardless of their sexuality or gender identity." The government and opposition opposed these amendments, with the government stating it supports marriage as a union between a man and a woman.

speeches.speaker: Chris Ellison
speeches.brief: The government moved a series of amendments to the Same-Sex Relationships (Equal Treatment in Commonwealth Laws—General Law Reform) Bill 2008, removing references to "the product of the relationship" in definitions of child and parent and instead referring to "a child of the person within the meaning of the Family Law Act," implementing recommendations from the Senate Standing Committee on Legal and Constitutional Affairs. The opposition supported the amendments, which also included changes to the Australian Citizenship Act for children born via artificial conception and surrogacy, and technical amendments to various other acts.
